reason: While the text describes a military defeat and records the elders of Israel asking 'Why has the Lord struck us today before the Philistines?', this is not a complaint about their leaders. The elders are questioning why God caused their defeat in battle, not criticizing Eli (the high priest/judge) or his sons. The subsequent action of fetching the Ark of the Covenant reflects the people's search for divine intervention in their military crisis, not dissatisfaction with their leadership. The text contains no explicit complaint against leaders or statements attributing blame to them for the defeat.
